notes.content: Французское издательство Nacon объявило о том, что оно вернуло права на выпуск видеоигр по лицензии WRC. Соглашение вступает в силу с 2027 года и завершится в 2032 году.

notes.title: Codemasters is "pausing development" on future rally games with its big re-acquisition of the WRC licence only having produced one game, which really sucks
notes.content:
That sound you can hear is me sighing into the steering wheel of my virtual Lancia Delta. Codemasters has announced that it's "pausing development plans on future rally titles" now it's finished adding stuff to EA Sports WRC, with the official WRC licence being revealed to moving on at the same time.

Read more

notes.title: EA не до WRC: Codemasters сворачивает разработку раллийных гонок
notes.content: Британская компания Codemasters, подконтрольная американскому издательству EA, объявила о пересмотре своих приоритетов. В результате было принято решение свернуть разработку раллийных игр. Анонс состоялся на фоне новостей о том, что руководство компании уволило около 400 человек.

notes.title: WRC 24 - Version 2.2.0 Patch Notes

The latest update for EA SPORTS™ WRC 24 is available to download from January 28, 2025. 
This update introduces the Le Maestros Content Pack, alongside a number of minor quality of life improvements and bug fixes.

[h2]Le Maestros Content Pack[/h2]

[previewyoutube=LRX-LmvuOqU;full][/previewyoutube]

Le Maestros is a tribute to the iconic era of French success, from the late 1990s to the late 2010s. French competitors won the World Drivers’ Championship a stunning 15 times in a row, as two of the greatest rally drivers of all time rose to ascendancy. 
This was also a highly successful time for French car manufacturers, with 11 World Manufacturers’ Championships and 11 drivers’ titles being taken behind the wheel of famed marques such as Citroën and Peugeot.
Le Maestros introduces new rally stages, Moments, liveries, historic vehicles and an all-new car class. 


[h2]New Livery Select Interface[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/0b4faa016bfe0dbb70b69c96e620c272cca495b4.jpg[/img]

We have refreshed the look and functionality of the livery selection screen when players choose a car to drive.
This new layout showcases designs with greater detail, while also making it easier to select liveries on cars with a large quantity of available designs.


[h2]Updated Homespace[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/81f8126b4f11cdcca05fbe62a9f0e4fbce15bbc8.jpg[/img]

We have refreshed the garage homespace of the game’s frontend menus with a fresh coat of paint, with the walls showcasing some of the new Le Maestros cars added to the game.
The game’s “splash screen” (which appears when you boot up the game) has also been updated with new artwork.


[h2]New Player Nationalities[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/ed4674363c43c447bbc42528abdc331ef7bd7557.jpg[/img]

We have added over 80 countries to the Driver Details menu, allowing more players from around the world to represent their nation in-game and on leaderboards.
The total number of selectable nationalities in the game is now above 170, covering the vast majority of EA SPORTS™ WRC players.


[h2]New Rally Pass Levels & Rewards[/h2]

We have extended the game’s Rally Pass, raising the level cap from 50 to 60.
In addition to this we have added 20 new livery editor decals as rewards, and rebalanced the XP earning rates and level requirements to account for the new level cap.

notes.title: WRC drivers react to EA SPORTS WRC™’s 24 Season Expansion
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=UeAmnT4sCcc;full][/previewyoutube]

Earlier this year at [url=https://www.goodwood.com/motorsport/festival-of-speed/explore/forest-rally-stage/]Goodwood Festival of Speed,[/url] we gave the stars of WRC an exclusive first hands-on with the EA SPORTS™ WRC 24 Season Expansion, featuring the current season’s cars and two new locations: ORLEN 80th Rally Poland and Tet Rally Latvia.
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UeAmnT4sCcc]Check out some early gameplay with our video here,[/url] and read on to see what they had to say about their experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/df13f04d1afe29471689c07b1a20f04bdca038c3.png[/img]

Hyundai’s Dani Sordo is one of the most experienced competitors in WRC history, with almost 200 rally starts to his name. He remarked on the authenticity of the game’s stages while speeding through Poland in the i20 N Rally1 HYBRID ‘24.
“It’s nice to practice the location here as you can remember the stage from real life,” he said. “It’s a new experience for me, I’m not so quick in the game yet! You need to be really focused to succeed. It’s really close to reality, though I’m faster in reality!”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/1037877daf1d7aee896a171313e72f2c7f6e1a9a.jpg[/img]

M-Sport’s Adrien Fourmaux has been the breakout star of 2024, taking the Ford Puma Rally1 HYBRID ‘24 to several podiums with his fearless driving. One feature of the Latvian stages stood out to him in particular.
“It looks a lot like the Latvian rally in real life” he remarked. “Like this chicane I’m coming up to, there’s a lot of them on the real stages.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/68dd5b0844b4b389975da1e5af0c0b1d70711f9b.jpg[/img]

Toyota’s Elfyn Evans, fresh off a second place finish at ORLEN 80th Rally Poland in real-life, felt right at home in the virtual version, with co-driver Scott Martin calling out the notes alongside.
“After some time with the game I have to say the nature of the stages is quite realistic, I immediately recognise a couple of places from the Rally in Poland last week. That’s great and the way the car reacts is similar to the real thing. It’s impressive.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/5996398aeb6469109f56c1f7c71427ba8fd20ea2.jpg[/img]

Elfyn’s team boss, Jari-Matti Latvala, also had a run on our Fanatec rig and highlighted the value of sim racing to younger drivers.
“The graphics really look amazing, a real authentic feeling with the roads,” he said. “I think for the newer generation, like the Japanese Challenge Programme we run at Toyota, it’s good to get this experience.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/250bb3b7d26f580e6505ef0743826ccf777e429a.jpg[/img]

M-Sport rookie Grégoire Munster picked up on the finer details of the new EA SPORTS™ WRC stages.
“Straight away with the environment you know you’re in Poland. You can see it on the surface of the gravel, it’s a bit more sandy and whiter than you find in other rallies.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/0c2fe40237fe9659a15fd15ce4a0b69919ca5bb3.jpg[/img]

Finally, Hayden Paddon, driver for Hyundai Customer Racing and 2023 ERC Champion, was enamoured with his time in the sim.
“It’s cool to experience it first-hand, and with those brand new Latvian stages, it feels like you’re there,"" he remarked. “The handling of the car is supreme. Definitely the best rally game I’ve played and I look forward to when the expansion’s officially released.”

[previewyoutube=EEheXDw8ojE;full][/previewyoutube]

The EA SPORTS™ WRC 24 Season Expansion is available from October 8.

notes.title: EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Gameplay Deep Dive
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=-K5nxKUXlTY;full][/previewyoutube]

EA SPORTS™ WRC offers over 600 km of unique rally stages spanning 18 locations, featuring an extensive lineup of cars from various eras of rally racing. 

Already one of the most extensive rally games, it’s set to become even better with the addition of the 2024 Season Expansion*, enhancing the definitive rally experience from Codemasters.


[h3]Rally Modes[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/0c2ffc732fc9e9002cd4e9ef515a8e2073cdf796.jpg[/img]

Our 2024 Season Expansion* brings the official cars, drivers, liveries, and locations from the latest FIA World Rally Championship season. Before diving into the new features, let's explore how to access the 2024 content.

In Championship Mode, you can race as and against up to 52 real drivers and crews from the 2024 World Rally Championship season. Compete across WRC, WRC2 and Junior WRC classes for glory.

When playing in the 2024 season events, the WRC class will use the [url=https://youtu.be/_XQeec-c9k4?t=278]new points system[/url] introduced in the real-world this year.

Bring the car home in a solid points-paying position on the opening leg of the rally, before risking it all on Super Sunday and the Power Stage to score vital bonus points.

In Career, you’ll build up your own rally team, with access to the 2024 cars as well as historic vehicles from the base game.

When you start a new Career save after October 8, you’ll be put into the 2024 calendar right away. 

If you’re an existing EA SPORTS™ WRC player who is progressing through Career right now, your current 2023 calendar season will continue as-is, before your next season changes over to the 2024 calendar, events and opponents.

In Time Trial, Clubs, and Quick Play, you’ll be able to race 2024 cars against the base game’s 2023 cars in their respective classes. This expands the number of competitive options available, while also keeping leaderboards unified across our most popular multiplayer modes.

In Clubs, players who do not have access to stages from the 2024 Season Expansion will skip those events when they appear on championship calendars, but can compete as normal across all base game locations.

In Quick Play Multiplayer, if the host of a lobby owns the 2024 Season Expansion and selects a DLC location for an event, all players will gain temporary access to that location for the current event.

Finally, our daily challenge system, Moments, inspired by WRC history, will allow players to relive key events from the current season.




[h3]Five New Cars[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/b0eff433dcf419e12b32b41813199d6c085f6069.jpg[/img]

The 2024 Season Expansion* introduces five new cars across the three main WRC categories: WRC, WRC2, and Junior WRC. 

The latest models from Toyota, Hyundai, and Ford come fully upgraded, featuring their official 2024 liveries and bodyworks for a fresh and polished look. 

To mirror the WRC competition the handling of the new Rally1 vehicles has been constructed to accurately replicate their real-world counterparts, providing the closest on-stage battles yet.

Reigning manufacturer champion Toyota brings an all-star lineup with full-time drivers Elfyn Evans and Takamoto Katsuta, joined by Sébastien Ogier and Kalle Rovanperä, all driving the GR Yaris Rally1 HYBRID.

Hyundai's upgraded i20 N Rally1 HYBRID has been a fierce rival to the 2023 champions. Thierry Neuville and Ott Tänak have been leading the charge, supported by multiple part-time drivers throughout the season.

Meanwhile, M-Sport Ford's young talents, Adrien Fourmaux and Grégoire Munster, have had an impressive campaign, with the upgraded Ford Puma Rally1 HYBRID securing multiple podium finishes.
New engine audio has been recorded for the Puma Rally1 HYBRID, with the Hyundai and Toyota vehicles receiving an update to their existing recordings.

This ensures players enjoy the most immersive and authentic onboard experience yet, truly feeling what it's like to drive these incredible machines.

We're also adding the Toyota GR Yaris Rally2 to the roster, allowing you to recreate the real-life battle between Škoda and Citroën in-game. 

Ensuring an authentic experience, we have recorded the Yaris’ unique 3-cylinder engine and refined the vehicle handling to replicate its nimble chassis and punchy torque, giving the WRC2 class a whole new flavour.

For Junior WRC, the brand-new Ford Fiesta Rally3 Evo for 2024 is ready for players to experience firsthand.

Junior WRC is the training ground of rallying’s future stars, and a great starting point for new players.

All 2023 cars from the base game will remain in EA SPORTS™ WRC for everyone to enjoy, and are not removed in favour of the 2024 machinery.



[h3]Two new locations[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/2f13560426fc8f4c639d7c966aeb874498f438a1.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/23dd3e029b6467c7605d0a63110e34eb6a5efe3b.jpg[/img]

To further enhance one of the most definitive rally experiences we have made, we're adding two brand-new locations: WRC Orlen 80th Rally Poland and WRC Tet Rally Latvia.

Rally Poland returns to the WRC after more than seven years, offering 12 stages, comprised of long 'hero stages' based on real roads, and their shorter, reversed variants. 

Świętajno, allows players to drive the full 18 km and experience what real WRC drivers do. 
The second hero stage, Gmina Mrągowo, provides one of the calendar's fastest yet most technical challenges.

Tet Rally Latvia made its WRC debut in 2024, bringing a new challenge to real-world drivers and players alike. 

Over 20km of real roads await you, across two authentically replicated “hero stages”, with their shortened and reversed variants resulting in 12 total stages for the location.

Vecpils is a 16km stage with narrow forest sections, and Podnieki is a 10km challenge set against the backdrop of the Latvian countryside.

Both locations can be raced across all game modes in any weather and time of day, from sunny skies to treacherous winter snow, offering a true test of skill in varying conditions.

All 2023 calendar locations from the base game will remain in EA SPORTS™ WRC for everyone to enjoy, along with multiple bonus locations based on iconic rally environments from around the world.



[h3]New Liveries & Crews[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/3d0d4ec56825c0e4e305a7702a592ec660090117.jpg[/img]

EA SPORTS™ WRC 24 will feature over 50 liveries and crews from the current FIA World Rally Championship season. 

All of these liveries are available to use across all supported game modes, and the real-world driver and co-driver pairings will act as AI opponents. 

You can also drive as them yourself in Championship Mode, replicating the 2024 season and its events. 
We’ve gone into more detail on the liveries and crews coming to each car in the WRC, WRC2 and Junior WRC classes, check out our companion article here.


[h3]Two New Content Packs[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/62fe5c9191b1f0ae022d20e46ce9e4993af01100.jpg[/img]

Players who pick up the Expansion will also get two additional themed content packs, free of charge. These will feature even more new content including historic cars, liveries, classic stages and unique Moments to experience. 

Here’s a taste of what’s to come, get a sneak peek of them in action at the end of our Deep Dive video:

‘Le Maestros’ allows players to experience classic stages on Rallye Monte Carlo and the iconic Fafe stage in Rally de Portugal and is set to release this winter, with more information on its content to be revealed soon.

‘Hard Chargers’ takes players to the Umea region of Rally Sweden and to the hillsides of EKO Acropolis Rally Greece, with brand new routes to experience in Spring 2025. Stay tuned for more information!


[h3]More EA SPORTS™ WRC Reveals Coming Soon[/h3]

Over the coming weeks we’ll be sharing more news, pics, video and gameplay about the upcoming content, as well as the full patch notes for the update (including bug fixes and tweaks that will benefit base game players)

Follow us wherever you get your news and see the reveals before anyone else.

Get ready to tackle diverse terrains with a mixture of Gravel and Asphalt surfaces. Dive into Latvia's rich rally culture, as this fresh addition promises unforgettable experience. 
Like all WRC locations, Rally Latvia boasts several kilometres of authentic roads, 12 unique stages, and a wide range of challenging terrains and weather conditions, offering the full spectrum of EA SPORTS™ WRC excitement.

notes.title: EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion Revealed
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=EEheXDw8ojE;full][/previewyoutube]

Experience the thrill of the 2024 rally season with new locations, rally stages, real-world liveries, in-game challenges and high-performance vehicles. 
The EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion Bundle* brings players up-to-date with the current year of the FIA World Rally Championship, featuring new content across all three classes, WRC, WRC2 and Junior WRC.
Get a taste of what’s to come on October 8 with our reveal trailer above, and check out the information below for more detail.

[h2]Locations & Car Content Pack: Out October 8[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/11e90ac83806be9a1aada024c44492f19c2ba07a.png[/img]

The headline addition is the Locations & Car Content Pack, which can either be purchased individually, or as part of the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion Bundle.
This Content Pack brings players up to date with the latest WRC season, featuring cars, liveries, drivers and locations from the current season.


[h2]New Location: Tet Rally Latvia[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/8205e7ef91a8ae6eb5bcc54b8f0a2023865ee34a.png[/img]

Embark on a thrilling new adventure with Tet Rally Latvia, the location that made its WRC debut in 2024. 
This exciting addition brings fresh challenges and breathtaking landscapes, making it a must-run rally for all enthusiasts. 
Prepare to navigate through the dynamic terrains and immerse yourself in the Latvian rally culture, as this new location sets the stage for unforgettable racing moments.
As with all locations, Rally Latvia features several kilometres of real roads, 12 individual stages, and all of the challenging terrain variety and weather conditions one comes to expect from EA SPORTS™ WRC.


[h2]New Location: Orlen 80th Rally Poland[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/ae4fb1fa258e78b6a62ebbb77468a95f7f989dd9.png[/img]

After a five-year hiatus, the iconic Orlen 80th Rally Poland made a triumphant return to the 2024 WRC calendar. 
This historic rally is renowned for its fast-paced gravel stages and passionate fanbase. 
With its rich heritage and thrilling routes, Rally Poland offers a unique and exhilarating challenge that both seasoned and new rally fans will eagerly anticipate. 
Rally Poland features multiple routes using over 27 unique kilometres of real roads.
Including shortened and reversed variants of its two main stages, players will race through 12 stages in total, each with multiple weather conditions, road surface changes and seasonal challenges to overcome.


[h2]5 New Cars[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/3a5ff84fabbc6ae25731b7df6a0213be0e60e1f5.png[/img]

The development race never stops, and all three WRC vehicle manufacturers have made great strides in the hunt for ultimate performance. 
Drive the very latest in Rally1 technology from Ford, Hyundai and Toyota, with hybrid power, advanced suspension systems, and aerodynamics strong enough to make you feel like a hero on the road.
In addition to the three new cars in the top class of competition, the all-new Toyota GR Yaris Rally2 makes its WRC2 debut, going toe-to-toe with its rivals.
In Junior WRC, the Ford Fiesta Rally3 Evo is the perfect platform for the stars of the future, with its enhanced power, agility and style.

Here are the five new cars you will get to drive as part of this Content Pack, all of which can compete against base game cars in their respective classes, across various game modes:

WRC:
[list]
[*] Ford Puma Rally1 HYBRID ‘24
[*] Hyundai i20 N Rally1 HYBRID ‘24
[*] Toyota GR Yaris Rally1 HYBRID ‘24
[/list]
WRC2:
[list]
[*] Toyota GR Yaris Rally2
[/list]
Junior WRC:
[list]
[*] Ford Fiesta Rally3 Evo
[/list]

[h2]52 New Liveries & Crews[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/030e2c8affae31bfbd4e2ae93c39746d7eea9852.png[/img]

In addition to the new cars and locations mentioned above, the Locations & Car Content Pack contains over 50 vehicle liveries, along with their respective crew members (ie: drivers and co-drivers).
These 2024 season liveries are available on all of the new cars, alongside several existing WRC2 cars from the base game (like Oliver Solberg’s WRC2 car, shown above), bringing them up to date with the current season.
All 52 crews will be selectable as drivable pairings in Championship Mode, as well as showing up as AI opponents across relevant game modes, such as Career, Moments and Quick Play.

The Locations & Car Content Pack can either be purchased individually, or as part of the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion Bundle.
If you’re coming in to EA SPORTS™ WRC for the very first time, EA SPORTS™ WRC 24 contains the base game as well as the three Content Packs, giving you everything in a single purchase.
Speaking of Content Packs, let’s look at what you’ll get to play with in the coming months.


[h2]Le Maestros Content Pack: Coming in Winter 2024/25[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/370004ab73ddb1cc0ce3601f4e80085b6e62ad9c.png[/img]

This Winter, the first of two themed Content Packs, will be arriving in Winter 2024/25 giving players more experiences to enjoy in-game. 
First up is Le Maestros, which will add two new routes to existing locations from the base game. 
Like many of our base game routes, these can also be driven in shortened and reversed variants, giving you multiple additional individual stages per location:

[h3]Rallye Monte Carlo: Briançonnet (14.55km)[/h3]
Embark on the thrilling Briançonnet roads with precision-testing esses, drops, narrow bridges, classic hairpins, and dynamic terrain. 
Navigate challenging slow sections, fast straights, winding dangers, exciting junctions, and varied widths against Monte Carlo's stunning vistas.

[h3]Vodafone Rally de Portugal: Fafe (11.18 km)[/h3]
Take on the iconic Fafe stage with its thrilling jumps and stunning Portuguese vistas. 
This meticulously recreated track features the renowned Fafe jump, pushing your skills to their limits.
Le Maestros also features additional content, which we will reveal closer to release. It can be purchased individually, or as part of the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion Bundle.

[h2]Hard Chargers Content Pack: Coming in Spring 2025[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/34b8a0ed99d1b00335c62d736e15fd4f869540cb.png[/img]

Kicking off the new year at full speed comes Hard Chargers, another themed Content Pack, releasing in Spring 2025.
As with Le Maestros, this adds new routes to base game locations, all of which can be driven in shortened and reversed variants.

[h3]Rally Sweden - Umea (10.08 km) & Umea Sprint (5.16 km)[/h3]
These fast, technical routes include long straights, sharp turns, strategic bumps, tree-lined paths, deforested sections, a tunnel, and the famed Red Barn Arena. 
With 4-5 metre road widths, it offers a dynamic, intense rally spectacle that tests your skills at every turn.

[h3]EKO Acropolis Rally Greece - Harvati (14.42 km)[/h3]
Harvati is a challenging mountain course with a winding start and river crossing, so expect water splashes as well as rocky, muddy, and gravel surfaces. 
Tackle road width changes, steep sections alongside farm buildings, dips, tight winding parts, and roadside trees. 
The final third opens up slightly before becoming winding and technical again, offering a thrilling and challenging driving experience.

Hard Chargers also features additional content, which we will reveal closer to release. It can be purchased individually, or as part of the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion Bundle

[h2]EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion FAQ[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/c79d1ac1fa90e9d05375905f76492d11deb59b6d.jpg[/img]

First-off, check out the comparison table above, as that covers the two most common scenarios, existing EA SPORTS™ WRC players and brand new players who want to get everything in a single purchase.

Buy the 2024 Season Expansion Bundle, which contains:
[list]

[h2]More EA SPORTS™ WRC Reveals Coming Soon
[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/57b6c5b3132c6e6344f956aaddeffc13eafb9b26.png[/img]

We’re just getting started with our run-up to the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion Bundle launch on October 8.
Over the coming weeks we’ll be sharing more news, pics, video and gameplay about the upcoming content, so be sure to follow us wherever you get your news and see the reveals before anyone else.

[list]
[*] Subscribe to our YouTube channel.

[/list]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1849250/EA_SPORTS_WRC/

notes.title: EA SPORTS™ WRC: 2024 Roadmap Revealed
notes.content:
Ever since the launch of EA SPORTS™ WRC last year, we’ve received tons of feedback from fans about the game, how they play, and what they would like to see in the future.

Today we can begin sharing what we’ve been working on, with the announcement of our 2024 Roadmap*, including exciting new content for rally fans to explore and enjoy.

Check out the roadmap and details below, and stay tuned over the coming months for much more detail on what’s to come for EA SPORTS™ WRC.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/577ebc1d9b8cd5cd97209ec697b829b2243546f8.jpg[/img]

[h2]EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion - Coming in October[/h2]

As the 2024 FIA World Rally Championship season heats up, we’re delighted to announce that the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion** will release in October.

This expansion pack will bring players up-to-date with the current season of the sport, featuring new locations, rally stages, high-performance vehicles, liveries and more.

Check back in the coming months as we dive into more detail on the expansion and reveal all of the content, ahead of its release.

Players who purchase the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion will also receive an additional two DLC packs** post-launch, more on those below.

[h2]EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Edition - Coming in October[/h2]

If you’ve never experienced the thrill of EA SPORTS™ WRC before, October will be the perfect time to start as we’ll also release a bundle for new players.

This standalone bundle combines the EA SPORTS™ WRC base game and the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion into a single purchase.

This also includes the two additional DLC packs (more info below) that will release post-launch.

[h2]EA SPORTS™ WRC DLC Packs - Coming this Winter & Spring[/h2]

Following the launch of the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion, two additional DLC packs will be released, the first coming this Winter and the second in Spring of 2025.

Players who purchase the EA SPORTS™ WRC 2024 Season Expansion will receive these at no extra cost, and those without the expansion can purchase the packs individually.

These themed DLC packs will contain new cars, additional rally stages for existing locations, moments, and more.

We’ll share more details later this year,[url=https://linktr.ee/easportswrc] follow us on social media [/url]to get the latest news.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/7b518326d04f42c707699ae618141fee433de618.jpg[/img]

[h2]EA SPORTS™ WRC Season 6 Rally Pass - Starts July 30[/h2]

Shifting gears towards the immediate future now, we’re pleased to announce that the Season 6 Rally Pass** begins next week, from July 30.

Based on player feedback received throughout the past year, we have made a number of changes to the Rally Pass, to improve the experience for all players.

For the first time, players can unlock liveries for cars outside of the WRC (Rally1) class, as well as additional sponsor decal sets for the livery editor.

Rewards will also be grouped, so that players can customise their driver with a complete set of new cosmetics, instead of sequentially unlocking each piece across multiple levels (as in Seasons 1-5).

Moments also return for Season 6, and the Season 6 Rally Pass will be free for all players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/aa706737edeb54e5b29caefc2e3ccebebbd9d76c.jpg[/img]

[h2]esports WRC - Coming Soon[/h2]

Finally, esports WRC is still in development and we’re almost ready to share the official competition information and event calendar, as we continue to work with our partners on the finer details of the series.

The 2024 season is expected to consist of online qualifiers[url=https://racenet.com/ea_sports_wrc] via Racenet,[/url] and an in-person final where the top players compete for the title of esports WRC World Champion. The series will challenge players across a range of locations and conditions in Rally1 cars.

Stay tuned for further updates, and as with all news you’ll get it first on [url=https://linktr.ee/easportswrc]our social media channels.[/url] In the meantime you can watch some high-intensity action from [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_a9LCDfY6-A]our invitational exhibition event,[/url] which was held in Poland at the end of 2023.

There’s never been a better time to jump in to EA SPORTS™ WRC, or return after some time away.

[url=https://www.ea.com/en-gb/games/ea-sports-wrc/wrc/ea-play]Try out the game for 5 hours with EA Play and unlock exclusive rewards in-game.[/url]

notes.title: EA SPORTS™ WRC - EA anticheat
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/254b3c7507e6060929a510be94107b3c739dd778.png[/img]

As part of our ongoing efforts to create a safe and fair experience for all players, we are adding EA anticheat to EA SPORTS™ WRC from June 2024.

Rally is a competitive sport where drivers battle against the clock, the car and the world for the best times on the leaderboards. 

Protecting the competitive integrity of our leaderboards is integral to providing a fun, fair and authentic rally experience for everyone.

For more information regarding EA anticheat, please see the FAQ below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/7f586d04b4139c0f1f23d3c102d88e4dad0eb08d.png[/img]

[h2]FAQ[/h2]
[h3]What is EA anticheat?[/h3]
EA anticheat is a kernel-mode anti-cheat and anti-tamper solution developed in-house at Electronic Arts. 

PC cheat developers have increasingly moved into the kernel, so we need to have kernel-mode protections to ensure fair play and tackle PC cheat developers on an even playing field. 

As tech-inclined video gamers ourselves, it is important to us to make sure that any kernel anti-cheat included in our games acts with a strong focus on the privacy and security of our gamers that use a PC. 

[h3]What platforms is EA anticheat available on?[/h3]
EA anticheat is used on the PC versions of EA SPORTS™ WRC. 

It is not required on Xbox Series X|S or PlayStation 5 versions of the game, which are protected by existing anti-cheat and anti-tamper solutions.

[h3]What game versions of EA SPORTS™ WRC feature EA anticheat?[/h3]
EA anticheat is a part of EA SPORTS™ WRC from Version 1.9.0 onwards.

The release date for the Version 1.9.0 update is to be confirmed, follow our social media channels for the latest news.

[h3]How do I install and troubleshoot EA anticheat?[/h3]
EA SPORTS™ WRC will attempt to install EA anticheat if it is not on your system already.
You can also install EA anticheat manually, please see our installation and troubleshooting FAQ for more information.

[h3]Why are you moving to EA anticheat?[/h3]
Third party anti-cheat solutions are often opaque to our teams, and prevent us from implementing additional privacy controls or customisations that provide greater accuracy and granularity for EA-specific game modes. 

With EA anticheat we have full stack ownership of the security & privacy posture, so we can fix security issues as soon as they may arise.

[h3]Why is kernel level anti-cheat needed?[/h3]
This varies on a game-by-game basis. 

For games that are highly competitive and contain many online modes such as EA SPORTS™ WRC, kernel-mode protection is absolutely vital. 

When cheat programs operate in kernel space, they can make their cheat functionally invisible to anti-cheat solutions that live in user-mode. 

Unfortunately, the last few years have seen a large increase in cheats and cheat techniques operating in kernel-mode, so the only reliable way to detect and block these is to continue to have our anti-cheat operate there as well. 

[h3]Are the System Requirements for EA SPORTS™ WRC changing?[/h3]
The minimum system requirements for EA SPORTS™ WRC specify Windows 10 as the operating system. This will not change.

Additionally, EA SPORTS™ WRC will not run on the native Steam OS for Steam Deck following the release of EA anticheat.

EA SPORTS™ WRC has officially been categorised as "Unsupported" on Steam Deck since its release in 2023.

[h3]Will EA anticheat degrade gameplay?[/h3]
No. 

We’ve conducted extensive internal and independent performance and stability assessments to ensure EA anticheat is as performant and lightweight as possible. 

EA anticheat will have no discernible impact on your gameplay.  

[h3]Does EA anticheat run when I start my PC, or only when the game is running?[/h3]
EA anticheat only runs when a game with EA anticheat protection included is running. 

All anti-cheat processes shut down when the game does.

[h3]Does EA anticheat stay on my PC if I uninstall EA SPORTS™ WRC? Can I uninstall it if I want?[/h3]
If you have uninstalled all of your EA games that have EA anticheat protection, EA anticheat will automatically uninstall and remove itself from your PC. 

It can also be manually uninstalled by you at any time you choose and will be completely removed from your PC. 

Please note that if you uninstall EA anticheat, any games that require EA anticheat protection will not be playable until EA anticheat is reinstalled. 

If you would like to reinstall EA anticheat we’ve made it as easy as possible to do so, with simple prompts in the game launch process.

[h3]Does EA anticheat let EA see my browsing history, personal files, or things like that?[/h3]
Player privacy is a top concern of our Game Security & Anti-Cheat team - after all, we’re players too. 
EA anticheat will only look at what it needs to for anti-cheat purposes in our games and we have limited the information EA anticheat collects. 

If you have a process on your PC that is trying to interact with our game, EA anticheat could see that and respond. However, everything else is off limits. 

EA anticheat does not gather any information about your browsing history, applications that are not connected to EA games, or anything that is not directly related to anti-cheat protection. 
We’ve worked with independent, 3rd party computer security and privacy services firms to ensure EA anticheat operates with data privacy top of mind.

For the information that EA anticheat does collect, we strive to maintain privacy where possible through a cryptographic process called hashing to create unique identifiers and discard the original information. 

Overall, EA anticheat’s use of your computer and data collection is consistent with EA’s User Agreement and Privacy and Cookie Policy.

[h3]How do I know that EA anticheat is not introducing any security vulnerabilities to my PC?[/h3]
Our Game Security & Anti-Cheat team is composed of some of the best security engineers in the world, and we are passionate about ensuring that our software does not cause any security vulnerabilities. 
Our anti-cheat engineering team performs daily testing and we continuously run security and penetration tests against EA anticheat internally. 

But don’t just trust our word on this.  We’ve also worked with independent, 3rd party security and privacy assessors to validate EA anticheat does not degrade the security posture of your PC and to ensure strict data privacy boundaries.

Although we’re confident that we’ve taken every possible precaution, we are monitoring and listening to any reports received to make sure that potential issues get addressed as quickly as possible.  

[h3]I think I found a security vulnerability with EA anticheat, who can I contact?
[/h3]If you believe you’ve found a vulnerability, please let us know by following our Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure process by emailing secure@ea.com right away. 

We take potential security issues seriously, and will work to fix them as quickly as we can.

[h3]Where can I get help if I run into issues with EA anticheat?[/h3]
If you need help to install and troubleshoot EA anticheat on your PC then you can visit our EA Help page.

notes.title: EA SPORTS™ WRC - VR Beta Details and FAQ
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=Yt_s8OY3BkY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Experience a new way to play [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] with the addition of VR Beta to PC, coming soon in the Version 1.8.0 Update.

Check out the details below for further information on what you can expect to see when the update releases.[/h3]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/6ce384ec6d024cf7b1b67528a53b2a54a966b5e0.jpg[/img]
[h1]Availability & Release Dates[/h1]

[h2]When will VR Beta release?[/h2]
The VR Beta for [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] will release as part of the Version 1.8.0 Update.
At the time of writing, the release date of v1.8.0 is expected to be on April 30. Keep an eye on our [url=https://linktr.ee/easportswrc]social media[/url] for the latest news.

[h2]Is VR Beta a separate DLC or purchase to the main game?[/h2]
No, it is directly integrated into the main game as an additional boot mode, and released as a free update.

[h2]Why is it called a beta?[/h2]
Our implementation of VR into [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] is referred to as VR Beta as it is a new project for our development team.

Previous VR implementations (like those seen in DiRT Rally and DiRT Rally 2.0) were built with the help of external partners, whereas for [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i], Codemasters have been developing VR in-house for the first time.

Due to the wide range of VR headsets available in the market, on top of the wide range of PC hardware specs in general, we currently cannot test for all possible scenarios and configurations.

[h2]Is VR Beta time-limited, and does it require a separate branch of the game?[/h2]
VR Beta is integrated into the main [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] game on PC, you will not need to join a separate beta branch on Steam for example.

There is no time limit or restriction on when VR Beta is available, any PC player with compatible hardware can launch [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] in VR, and VR will not be removed from the game going forward.

When we are confident enough to say that VR is in a fully completed state, we will no longer refer to it as VR Beta.

[h2]Where is VR Beta available?[/h2]
[i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] VR Beta is available on PC (Steam, Epic, EA App), through compatible headsets.

If you have a compatible VR headset connected, you will be asked whether you want to play in VR or non-VR mode when you boot up the game.

[h2]Will VR Beta come to console?[/h2]
There are currently no plans to add VR to [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] on console in any capacity, Beta or otherwise.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/4883b1201b220c790d2d863ced961946edc912f3.jpg[/img]
[h1]Hardware Support[/h1]

[h2]What VR headsets are supported in [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i]?[/h2]
Using OpenXR technology via Unreal Engine, a wide range of headsets should be compatible with [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i].

Additionally, we have tested and can confirm the following headsets are supported:

[list]
[*] Meta Quest 3
[*] Meta Quest 2
[*] Meta Quest Pro
[*] Valve Index
[*] Oculus Rift S
[*] Oculus CV1
[*] HTC Vive
[/list]

The following are considered “partially supported” at this time:

[list]
[*] HTC Vive Cosmos
[*] HTC Vive Pro 2
[/list]
OpenXR based Headsets not listed above (and not on the “not supported list” below) may work, but we cannot guarantee full functionality at this time.

[h2]What VR hardware is NOT supported in [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i]?[/h2]
The following headsets are not supported:

[list]
[*] PlayStation VR 
[*] PlayStation VR 2
[*] Apple Vision Pro
[/list]

3D tracked controllers are not officially supported, we recommend people drive with the same peripherals they would use in non-VR (steering wheel, controller, keyboard etc.).

[h2]What are the minimum and recommended PC hardware requirements for playing in VR?[/h2]
The “minimum specs” for playing in VR are equivalent to the “recommended specs” for non-VR. You can find those here but for clarity:

[olist]
[*] Operating System: Windows 10
[*] CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 3700X or Intel i5 10600K
[*] GPU: AMD Radeon RC 5700XR or NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070
[*] RAM: 16 GB
[*] DirectX: Version 12 (“DX12”)
[*] Storage: 95GB, SSD preferred
[*] Network: Broadband internet connection (to download updates, game is playable offline)
[*] Other hardware: Monitor and keyboard
[/olist]

Additionally, below are some configurations we have tested and confirmed to achieve optimal performance during gameplay.

Configuration 1: 90+ fps achieved
[list]
[*] Headset: Meta Quest 2
[*] CPU: Intel i9 13900K
[*] GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (4090 also tested)
[*] RAM: 32 GB
[*] In-Game Upscaler Setting: DLSS Quality
[*] In-Game Graphics Preset: Ultra
[/list]
Configuration 2: 90+ fps achieved
[list]
[*] Headset: Meta Quest 2
[*] CPU: AMD Ryzen R9 7900x
[*] GPU: AMD RX 7900XT
[*] RAM: 32 GB
[*] In-Game Upscaler Setting: FidelityFX Quality
[*] In-Game Graphics Preset: High
[/list]
Configuration 3: 80+ fps achieved
[list]
[*] Headset: Meta Quest 2
[*] CPU: Intel i9 10900K
[*] GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080
[*] RAM: 32 GB
[*] In-Game Upscaler Setting: DLSS Quality
[*] In-Game Graphics Preset: High
[/list]
Any higher spec hardware than this will result in a more performant experience, and give greater freedom to use more demanding graphics settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/c63802bb8a4f5601502e5e8ba5588b74b4b1f48c.png[/img]
[h1]Getting Started[/h1]

[h2]How do I launch the game in VR while using a Meta Quest device?[/h2]
[list]
[*] Turn on the headset.
[*] In the Oculus app, go to [b]Settings > General > Set Meta Quest Link as active OpenXR.[/b]
[*] Connect the cable between your headset and PC.
[*] Open Notifications from Quest device, and select [b]Enable Quest Link.[/b]
[*] If a dialogue box pops up on the headset, click [b]Enable [/b]to start playing.
[*] If not, enable manually via the Oculus Home screen:[b] Quick Settings > System > Quest Link > Launch Quest Link.[/b]
[*] Alternatively, again via Oculus Home screen:[b] Quick Settings > Launch Quest Link > Select PC > Connect.[/b]
[*] Once your headset is connected, launch [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i].
[/list]

[h2]What are the optimal launch settings when using the Meta Quest App?[/h2]
We recommend using a USB 3.0 cable in order to experience better performance. Please note that we currently do not support Air Link.

We also recommend you set your refresh rate to 90hz within the Oculus App, this can be done via Devices > Advanced > Graphics Settings.

[h2]How do I launch the game in VR while using an HTC device?[/h2]
[list]
[*] Ensure all wired connections are done correctly.
[*] Make sure the base station can see the headset.
[*] Open Vive Console and let it detect the headset.
[*] Go to Vive Console > Settings > Advanced > OpenXR > Steam OpenXR and ensure Application Experience is set to VR
[*] Open Steam VR and select Update Permissions if/when prompted.
[*]  Launch [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] from the PC, or via Steam VR home in the headset.
[/list]

[h2]How do I launch the game in VR while using an HP device?[/h2]
[list]
[*] Ensure all wired connections are done correctly.
[*] Download and open [url=https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9ng1h8b3zc7m?hl=en-gb&gl=GB]Mixed Reality Portal[/url].
[*] A popup may appear saying that “Windows Mixed Reality is not set up to run OpenXR apps”. If so, select Fix It.
[*] Alternatively, launch SteamVR and select [b]Update Permissions[/b] if/when prompted.
[*] Launch [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] from the PC, or via desktop available within the headset.
[/list]

[h2]What are the optimal launch settings when using the Mixed Reality Portal?[/h2]

We recommend adjusting the [b]Frame Rate[/b] and [b]Display Resolution[/b] to the best quality available.

To change these settings, go to [b]Expand > See More > Settings > Mixed Reality > Headset Display.[/b]

[h2]What are the optimal launch settings when using SteamVR?[/h2]
We recommend disabling automatic resolution scaling and setting headset [b]Resolution Per Eye [/b]manually.

This can be done by setting [b]Render Resolution[/b] to [b]Custom [/b]and then adjusting the slider beneath.

Ideally, [b]Resolution Per Eye[/b] should be set to match the values your headset provides, though you can increase it beyond that until you see performance issues, in order to experience super-sampled anti-aliasing.

To improve performance you can try lowering the [b]Resolution Per Eye [/b]setting until you achieve a frame rate you are happy with.

[h2]Should I enable Motion Smoothing when using SteamVR?[/h2]
If you are experiencing inconsistent frame rates, you may want to try enabling Motion Smoothing via the SteamVR settings.

To learn more about Motion Smoothing in Steam VR, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/250820/announcements/detail/1705071932992003492]please see this article on the Steam website.[/url]

Motion Smoothing is a feature that attempts to insert frames if [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] drops a frame. 

This causes an impact to overall FPS however it ensures a smoother, more consistent experience, albeit at a lower framerate. Additionally, this may cause some visual effects or assets to take on a corrupted appearance.

[h2]Should I enable Asynchronous Spacewarp when using a Meta Quest device?[/h2]
If you are experiencing inconsistent frame rates, you may want to try enabling Asynchronous Spacewarp via the Oculus Debug Tool.

To do this, head to [b]C:\Program Files\Oculus\Support\oculus-diagnostics, open OculusDebugTool[/b] and look for [b](PC) Asynchronous Spacewarp[/b].

Asynchronous Spacewarp is a feature that attempts to insert frames if [i]EA SPORTS™ WRC[/i] drops a frame. 

This causes an impact to overall FPS however it ensures a smoother, more consistent experience, albeit at a lower framerate. Additionally, this may cause some visual effects or assets to take on a corrupted appearance.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/5b6cb6fd05b05de61a7d874bd616334ff159e965.jpg[/img]

[h1]Settings & Comfort[/h1]

[h2]What Graphical Settings are available in VR Beta?[/h2]
VR players will have access to a number of settings to help further optimise their playing experience.

Below are some settings we recommend players start with as a baseline, and then adjust to match the capabilities of their specific headset and PC hardware.

If framerates and performance are good on your system, try setting some of these higher for a more detailed visual experience.

Depending on your hardware, some Basic Graphics settings may not be adjustable when playing the game in VR.

Motion Blur setting is also mirrored in the Accessibility menu, the setting applied in either location affects both.

Basic Graphics:
[list]
[*] Resolution: Varies based on headset used
[*] Display Mode: Matches the player’s non-VR mode preference (Windowed etc.), to be applied to the PC monitor feed outside of the headset
[*] Anti-Aliasing Quality: Low
[*] VSync: On
[*] Anisotropic Filtering: x4
[*] Main Menu Framerate: Off
[*] Upscaler: Off
[*] Foveation Strength: 3
[/list]

Advanced Graphics:
[list]
[*] Shadows: Low
[*] Fog: Off
[*] Particles: Low
[*] Weather: Low
[*] Crowd: Ultra Low
[*] Ground Cover: Ultra Low
[*] Trees: Low
[*] Dynamic Objects: Low
[*] Car Reflections: Ultra Low
[*] Post-Process Quality: Ultra Low
[*] Mirrors: Off
[*] Skidmarks: Off
[*] Track: Low
[*] Textures: Low
[*] Shaders: Low
[*] Motion Blur: Off
[/list]

[h2]What is a good refresh rate and resolution to aim for when playing in VR?[/h2]
A smooth and consistent framerate will be the most comfortable and enjoyable when you play.

As a baseline, try to aim for a consistent 90hz, and change graphics settings if this cannot be achieved with the default configuration.

Headset resolution is not set in-game, you will need to make adjustments via your specific headset’s settings to find a good balance between visual fidelity and performance.

Resolution settings in-game affect the 2D display on your PC monitor. Reducing the 2D monitor’s resolution via in-game settings may result in slightly improved headset performance.

[h2]What gameplay and comfort settings are available in VR Beta?[/h2]

A number of VR settings are available to help players find a comfortable balance and reduce the potential for motion sickness.

Settings that are known to have the most significant impact on comfort also display a warning message within the menu.

On/Off Settings:
[list]
[*] 3D Location Reveal: 
This sets whether the location reveal is presented in full 3D or displayed on the virtual monitor.
[*] Recentre View on Boot: 
This sets whether the headset view is automatically re-centred when VR mode is first engaged
[*] Recentre View on Stage Start: 
This sets whether the headset view is automatically re-centred before the stage countdown begins.
[*] Toggle Driver Avatar: 
This sets whether the driver's body can be seen whilst racing in the driver's eye camera viewpoint.
[*] All Driving Views: 
This sets whether the camera can be changed to a view other than the driver's eye viewpoint.
[*] Toggle Car in Bonnet View: 
This sets whether the car model is visible when driving in bonnet view.  'All Driving Views' must also be set to 'On' to make this camera available.
[*] Fixed Horizon: 
This sets whether, when driving, the view of the world remains fixed and level, or whether it rotates with the position of the vehicle.
[*] Manual Camera Control: 
This sets whether the camera orientation can be affected by any other means than moving the headset.
[*] Toggle Look Back: 
This sets whether the option to look backwards, while driving, is enabled.
[/list]

Slider Settings:
[list]
[*] Crash Vignette: 
This changes the intensity of the vignette effect that covers the outside edge of the view during significant crashes. 
'0' turns the effect off completely.
[*] HUD Scale: 
This changes the overall size of the 'heads-up display' during racing. 
All components that make up this display, scale with that change. 
The larger the number the larger the size of the display.
[*] HUD Position: 
This changes the position of the 'heads-up display' during racing, up or down, in the view. 
The larger the number the higher the display will appear.
[*] HUD Distance: 
This changes the position of the 'heads-up display' during racing, towards or away from the initial view point. 
The larger the number the further away the display will appear.
[*] Virtual Monitor Scale: 
This changes the overall size of the 'virtual monitor' that displays the game when not driving. 
[*] All menu components, within this display, scale with that change. 
The larger the number the larger the size of the display.
[*] Virtual Monitor Position: 
This changes the position of the 'virtual monitor', that displays the game when not driving, up or down in the view. 
The larger the number the higher the display will appear.
[*] Virtual Monitor Distance: 
This changes the position of the 'virtual monitor', that displays the game when not driving, towards or away from the initial view point. 
The larger the number the further away the display will appear.
[/list]

[h2]Can the camera view be reset?[/h2]
Yes. The functionality varies depending on the headset used, but there is an option to Reset VR View to the default position.

This can also be mappable via the Input Bindings menu, the default keyboard key is F9.

Additionally, as mentioned above, there are also settings to automatically recentre view on boot, and at the start of every stage.

[h2]Are there any additional comfort features?[/h2]
A “take a break” reminder message is displayed in a number of non-driving areas of the game after 60 minutes of continued VR play.

This can be dismissed each time, or alternatively dismissed for the rest of your play session.

Additionally, as mentioned in the settings section above, there are a number of settings that can help improve comfort levels, the most notable being Fixed Horizon and Crash Vignette.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44592176/157884b1f6cc465918e5608bcf54a738af6b27fc.jpg[/img]

[h1]View Modes & Features[/h1]

[h2]Are any non-driving scenes rendered in 3D?[/h2]
Yes, players will be able to view the location reveal scene of each rally stage in a full 3D view.

This provides a fully immersive experience similar to standing by the road on a real stage. 

It can also be disabled in the Options & Settings menu for those who wish to proceed to the Service Area more quickly.

All other non-driving scenes and menus are rendered in 2D via a Virtual Monitor and viewable from within the headset.

[h2]Is there a complementary 2D render on the PC monitor when playing in VR?[/h2]

Yes, when playing in VR the PC monitor will display a representative 2D version, including menus.

This is useful for menu navigation without needing to wear the headset, and also for players who wish to record or broadcast their game on Twitch or YouTube.

Please note that the displayed resolution of the 2D render on the PC monitor may differ from the 3D view rendered within the headset.

In all 2D scenes, the Virtual Monitor from within the headset is replicated on the PC monitor. 

For 3D scenes (ie: when driving and during stage reveal if enabled), the view from only one eye is displayed on the PC monitor.


[h2]Can VR players play in multiplayer modes with non-VR players?[/h2]
Yes.

[h2]Are any features not available in VR?[/h2]
Due to technical limitations, Photo Mode is not available at launch when the game is booted up in VR mode.

We are currently investigating ways to implement Photo Mode into VR, and if we find a solution will enable Photo Mode in VR via a future update.

[h2]Are there any “known issues” with VR Beta at launch?[/h2]
As of v1.8.0’s release (and at the time of this FAQ’s publication), these are the issues we have been investigating and will aim to resolve as soon as possible:

[list]
[*] Game may crash if the player frequently changes the Display Mode (Alt+Enter) during the “Enabling VR” dialogue screen.
[*] Game may crash if the player turns the PC monitor off and on again while VR is active.

notes.title: Information Regarding Career Mode Crashes
notes.content:
Hello players,
Following the v1.4.0 update to EA SPORTS™ WRC, an [url=https://answers.ea.com/t5/Bug-Reports/Game-crashes-when-clicking-quot-Continue-Career-quot/td-p/13310505]unforeseen issue with Career Mode[/url] has occurred that is affecting a number of players.
Please see below for further information and what we are doing to resolve it for you all.

[h2]What happened:[/h2]
[list]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1849250/view/3855707727958747596?l=english]The v1.4.0 update was released.[/url]
[*] This update added Central European Rally to the game.
[*] Central European Rally was also added to Career Mode, both as part of the WRC class, and across several other Championships and Events in Career.
[*] The addition of Central European Rally caused a mismatch in the game code with a specific set of Benefactor objectives.
[*] Affected players will experience a 100% crash rate if their Career Mode save features these specific objectives.
[/list]

[h2]How are players affected:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Career Mode contains hundreds of combinations of Benefactor objectives, specifying which Events and Championships the player must compete in as progression targets.
[*] These Benefactor objectives are randomly assigned to players at the start of each Career Mode Season.
[*] Players who have specific combinations of these Benefactor objectives will experience a game crash if they attempt to continue their Career.
[*] Players who have not started Career, or start a new Career are not affected in Career Mode Season 1.
[*] Some players may be able to load a Career Mode save without any issue, though this cannot be predicted in advance.
[*] Players who are currently in Career Mode Season 2 and beyond in WRC2 and Junior WRC are at risk of a crash if they attempt to continue their career.
[*] Players who are currently in Career Mode Season 2 and beyond in WRC are also at risk, and players in Season 3 and beyond are at a higher risk.
[*] If a player has experienced this crash, there is a chance that their Career Mode progress has been lost with no ability to recover.
[/list]

[h2]How players can mitigate the issue:[/h2]
[list]
[*] If a player has an active Career Mode save, we are advising all players to avoid playing in Career until an update is released.
[*] With the hotfix we are aiming to restore existing Career Mode Saves for those that do not start a new Career.
[*] If a player wishes to start a new Career, they can do so without being affected by this issue, however their previous save will be permanently lost.
[/list]

[h2]How we are fixing the issue:[/h2]
[list]
[*] This issue is the #1 priority for our team as regards fixes and updates.
[*] However, as this is a complicated and delicate issue that affects save games, we do not wish to rush a quick fix, and inadvertently cause further issues down the line.
[*] With this hotfix we are also aiming to recover lost Career Mode saves for those that do not start a new Career.
[*] The aim is to have a hotfix ready as soon as possible.
[/list]

[h2]What else will be in the hotfix:[/h2]
[list]
[*] The primary goal of the hotfix will be to resolve the issues causing Career Mode to crash for players.
[*] In addition, we believe we have found a fix for the commonly-reported “inconsistent AI performance when resuming an Event” issue.
[*] We plan to implement this AI change into the hotfix as well, thank you for your recent reports which have helped us to potentially diagnose the root cause.
[*] Finally, we plan to implement a fix to the track limits issue reported on Rally Chile stages, which arose after the v1.4.0 update was released.
[/list]

[h2]When will a hotfix be released:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Due to the complexity of the Career Mode issue, the action required to resolve it, and the time required for testing and certification, we aim to be in a position to issue a hotfix on all platforms in mid January.
[/list]

notes.title: PC Performance
notes.content:
With an upcoming update to WRC, we have been working hard to address the performance issues some players are reporting on PC.

The team has been implementing Unreal's PSO system (shader-precompiling) which will address many of the stalls experienced by players in the first run of a track in various weather conditions. Alongside this, we have also targeted specific locations where framerate is sub-optimal and focussed our efforts on these areas.

The upcoming patch also contains many other fixes and optimizations. The team continues to work on optimizations for future updates.

This patch is coming soon. Follow EA SPORTS WRC for the latest news and patch information.
